through the different nodes to find a

And when it comes to traversing a tree, when
you're building your own tree,
you can implement this search algorithm
in 2 different ways. There are 2 ways of
searching for something in a tree. There are
2 ways of moving through a tree. You can go
through a tree
depth-first and breadth-first. Now what's
the difference?
If you explore a tree depth-first, if you're
looking for an element depth-first, you
first of all go down an entire path in your
tree like this, all the orange nodes,
and then only once you explored an entire
path you move to the sibling nodes in that
branch you're looking at and later also the
other branches you got in your tree.
Now, if you're looking for something
breadth-first,
you take a different approach. There, you
don't dig into one path and drill deeply
into the tree immediately.
Instead, you simply move through different
siblings on one level and only if you don't
find your element there,
you look into the next level and go through
the siblings there. So these are really just
2 different ways of traversing a tree, of
moving through a tree to find something. Now
let's add a search algorithm, a find method
to our basic tree here, and let's implement
it in both ways so that we can get a feeling
for how it looks like. And of course, I'll
thereafter also share some information about
when to use which approach.
